course.name: Shibuya, Daikanyama & Nakameguro
course.tag: Downhill to the river
course.why: Start in the noise, then walk 20 minutes downhill into the quiet part: the Daikanyama bookshop, then the Meguro river and its cafés. Easy pace, good for talking.
steps: Cross once, then follow the river side of the station.
20 minutes, mostly downhill, through a residential area.
Tsutaya Books, three buildings of books and a lounge. Log Road is a garden path on an old rail line with a brewery.
Ivy Place or Spring Valley Brewery. See the picks below.
Pick one of the four coffee spots below.
The Hibiya line goes straight to Hibiya and Ginza.
course.moves: Everything on foot, about 3 km in total. Shibuya → Daikanyama 20 min. Daikanyama → Nakameguro 15 min. Nakameguro station has the Hibiya and Toyoko lines.
food: Pancakes, salads and pasta in the T-Site garden. Weekend queue, so we put our name down first.
Kirin’s brewery restaurant on Log Road. Beer flight and a proper lunch.
A small roaster right by the station. Upstairs seats look out over the Toyoko line trains.
On the river path under the cherry trees. They roast beans and bake pastries on site.
Run by a world latte art champion, in a quiet concrete building. Known for latte art and cheesecake.
The big four-floor roastery, about 10 minutes upriver.
course.good: Flat and easy the whole way, on quiet streets. Plenty of time to talk.
course.mind: The Meguro river cherry trees are green in October, not pink. We finish at Nakameguro station at 15:30.

course.name: Edo and Hokusai
course.tag: Course A · Ryogoku, across the river
course.why: One train ride east, into the old low city. A museum that rebuilds Edo at full size, a sumo neighbourhood for lunch, a small garden, and Hokusai at the end.
steps: Shimbashi is 3 minutes on foot. Ryogoku is about 20 minutes by train.

Reopened in March 2026 after four years of rebuilding. A full-size Nihonbashi bridge you walk across, Edo townhouses you step into, and the city model with thousands of small figures. 800 yen, 400 if you are 65 or over.
The sumo stew, in the streets where the wrestlers live. Five minutes from the museum.
Free, small, and empty on a weekday. A tidal pond garden from the 1690s.
Hokusai was born in this neighbourhood. 400 yen, 300 if you are 65 or over. The audio guide is 500 yen and runs on your own phone, so bring earphones.
Or ten more minutes east to Tokyo Skytree if you still have legs.
course.moves: Hotel to Ryogoku about 20 minutes by train (Toei Oedo line from Shiodome, or JR from Shimbashi via Akihabara). Everything in Ryogoku is within a 10-minute walk of everything else.
food: The sumo hot pot. Lunch 11:30 to 14:30, small pot set from 1,000 yen, the full Ryogoku chanko set 1,700 yen.
Run by a former ozeki. Lunch is weekdays only and they close on Mondays, so this one works on Tuesday or Wednesday.
course.good: Museums, and seeing what Edo actually looked like before it became Tokyo. Mostly indoors, so rain does not matter.
course.mind: Both museums close on Mondays. The Sumida river boats from Ryogoku are suspended at the moment, so we use the train, not the water.

course.name: A day with your hands
course.tag: Course B · Tsukiji and Ginza
course.why: The ink painting and the tea ceremony from your list, both close to the hotel. You paint in the morning, eat in Tsukiji, and sit down to tea in the afternoon a minute from the Kabukiza.
steps: 15 minutes on foot from the hotel. The selling hours are 9:00 to 14:00. Tuesday is an open day; Wednesday is a market holiday and many shops stay shut.
One hour in a teahouse on the second street of Tsukiji, with an English-speaking teacher, eight people at most. You take your paper home.
Tamagoyaki, grilled fish, sushi at a counter. See the picks below.
45 minutes, in English, right beside the Kabukiza. 3,500 yen each in a shared room, 5,000 yen each if we take the room privately. On the hour, 10:00 to 17:00, open every day.
12 minutes to the hotel, through the back streets of Ginza rather than the main avenue.
Bar Doulton in Ginza 6-chome, over a thousand bottles, weekdays 18:00 to midnight. Closed on Sundays.
course.moves: All of it on foot. Hotel to Tsukiji 15 minutes, Tsukiji to the tea room 10 minutes, tea room to hotel 12 minutes.
food: Eat standing up from the stalls: tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, uni. Selling hours 9:00 to 14:00, and Wednesday is a market holiday.
Not food, but the 45 minutes is the point. Next door to the theatre, English, chairs can be arranged if kneeling is not for you.
course.good: You leave with something you made, and the tea room is one minute from the theatre you are already visiting on Sunday.
course.mind: Both classes are by reservation and I book them, so tell me the day. The ink painting studio in Aoyama I also looked at only runs Friday to Monday, which is why I put the Tsukiji one here.

course.name: Ginza at your own pace
course.tag: Course C · No trains at all
course.why: A garden by the water, matcha in a teahouse on an island, and the shops of Ginza. Everything inside a 20-minute walk of your room, so you can stop whenever you like.
steps: A shogun duck-hunting garden with a tidal pond, 15 to 18 minutes on foot from the hotel. 300 yen, 150 if you are 65 or over. Open 9:00 to 17:00.
The teahouse in the middle of the pond serves matcha with a sweet. You sit on tatami with the skyline behind the pines.
Walk back up into the city and pick a floor of a department store, or a counter in a side street.
Itoya for paper and pens, the food halls in the basements, Mitsukoshi and Wako on the corner.
The basement floor under the theatre is open to anyone: sweets, fans, prints, a coffee shop. The roof garden on the fifth floor is free as well.
Twelve minutes from the theatre, and you are already home.
course.moves: All on foot. Hotel to Hamarikyu 15 to 18 minutes, Hamarikyu to Ginza 15 minutes, Ginza to the Kabukiza 8 minutes, Kabukiza to the hotel 12 minutes.
food: The teahouse on the island. Matcha with a seasonal sweet, prices on the day.
Twelve floors of stationery, with a cafe near the top. Good for presents.
course.good: A slow day with no train, no timetable, and a bench whenever you want one.
course.mind: On Sunday 4 October the main avenue of Ginza is closed to cars from 12:00 to 17:00, which is why this course fits the afternoon after the kabuki. The garden has free English volunteer guides at 11:00, but only at weekends.

course.name: The market at dawn, tea by noon
course.tag: Market, garden, matcha
chips: Jet lag works in your favour
course.why: On day three the clock still has you awake at five, so we use it instead of fighting it. A fish market is on your interest list and so is a tea ceremony, and both sit within two kilometres of your hotel. You are back by early afternoon with the evening free to pack for Hakone.
steps: Ten minutes by taxi. You will most likely be awake anyway.
Four blocks, around four hundred shops, at the hour the cooks are still buying. Tamagoyaki straight off the grill, scallops on the shell, dried bonito shaved in front of you. We eat as we walk.
A sit-down bowl once the walking is done.
Ten minutes on foot. A 400-year-old shogun’s garden with saltwater ponds, sitting inside the modern skyline. Flat paths, benches all the way round.

A tea house standing out over the pond on stilts. Matcha whisked in front of you with a seasonal sweet, sitting on tatami with the water on three sides. The closest thing to a tea ceremony that needs no booking.
A twenty-minute walk or a short taxi. The afternoon is yours.
course.moves: Hotel → Tsukiji 10 min by taxi. Market on foot. Market → garden 10 min on foot. Garden → hotel about 20 min on foot.
food: Tsukiji · grilled egg on a stick
The egg stand people queue at from nine in the morning. Warm, sweet, a hundred yen, eaten standing up. The right first bite of the market.
Tsukiji · beef and offal over rice
A market stall with a few stools, simmering the same pot since the 1940s. The workers’ breakfast, not a tourist dish.
If you want a table and a chair rather than a stool: tuna bowls and grilled fish, with a menu in English.
course.good: Uses the jet lag instead of fighting it, and gives you the whole afternoon back before the Hakone train.
course.mind: Sunday closes some of the market. Knives are better bought on Oct 6 — see course D — so you are not carrying a blade around Japan for three weeks.

course.name: Edo Tokyo and Hokusai
course.tag: Two museums, ten minutes apart
course.why: Your interest list says “Edo Tokyo museum / Hokusai museum”. They are in the same neighbourhood, a ten-minute walk apart, and Sunday is the day both are open. Ryogoku is also the sumo district, which makes it a useful warm-up for Osaka on the 28th.
steps: About 25 minutes by train. A late start after the baseball.

You enter by walking across a full-size replica of the old Nihonbashi bridge, and the city unfolds underneath: a whole Edo street, a tenement house you can step into, then the earthquake, the war and the neon years. Two hours, all indoors, benches and lifts throughout. 800 yen.
The stew sumo wrestlers eat to build weight, served in the streets where they train.

Ten minutes on foot. Hokusai was born here and moved house ninety-three times without leaving the area. The Great Wave, the views of Fuji, and the sketchbooks where you can watch the brush thinking. This is the ink painting on your list, at its source.
The national sumo arena is across the street, with the handprints of past champions outside. The garden beside it is free, small and almost empty.
About 25 minutes by train, in time to pack for Hakone.
course.moves: Hotel → Ryogoku about 25 min by train. Museum → lunch 5 min on foot. Lunch → Hokusai museum 10 min. Hokusai → arena and garden 8 min. Ryogoku → hotel about 25 min.
food: Run by a former ozeki. The chicken-broth pot is the one his stable actually ate. Reservations help on a Sunday.
Ryogoku · chanko in an old stable
You eat around the real training ring of the old Miyagino stable, still in the middle of the room. The building alone is worth the walk.
A restored station building with a full-size sumo ring in the middle and a dozen restaurants around it. Good if you each want something different.
course.good: Two things off the interest list in one afternoon, both indoors, both a short walk apart. The best possible preparation for the sumo on Sept 28.
course.mind: Both museums usually close on Mondays, so the 20th is the day this works. Tickets are sold at the door. Nothing here needs booking except the chanko table.

course.name: Meiji shrine and a Sunday in the park
course.tag: Daylight, brass bands, rockabilly
course.why: Music and dance are on your list and nothing else on the trip covers them. Sunday is the one day Yoyogi Park fills with people playing, and the shrine forest next door is the flattest good walk in Tokyo.
steps: About 20 minutes by train to Harajuku.
A wide gravel path through a man-made forest of 100,000 donated trees, benches the whole way. On a Sunday morning you often catch a wedding procession crossing the courtyard under a red umbrella.
The park next door is where Tokyo goes to practise in public on Sundays: brass bands, drum circles, and the rockabilly dancers who have been meeting at the entrance since the 1980s.
Ten minutes on foot, away from the crowd.
The scramble crossing from above, then the quiet back streets. We stop when you have had enough.
About 20 minutes by train, in time to pack for Hakone.
course.moves: Hotel → Harajuku about 20 min by train. Shrine walk 10 min each way. Park next door. Park → Omotesando 10 min on foot. Omotesando → Shibuya 12 min on foot. Shibuya → hotel about 20 min.
food: Breaded pork cutlet in a converted 1920s bathhouse. Sit-down, quiet, easy to order.
The stand that started the Harajuku crepe in 1976. Thirty fillings on a photo menu, eaten while walking.
You order on a tablet and the plates arrive on a rail at your seat. Cheap, fast, and quietly entertaining.
course.good: Daylight and live music, and nothing to book. Easy to shorten at any point.
course.mind: The Sunday performers are not on a schedule, so they are a bonus rather than a promise. This is the most walking of the three.

course.name: Knives, and something to take home
course.tag: Kappabashi and Asakusa
chips: The one day the knife street is open
course.why: Knife sharpening is on your list, and this is the day to do it. Kappabashi’s knife shops close on Sundays, so Sept 20 was never going to work — and buying a blade at the start would mean carrying it through Hakone, Takayama, Kanazawa, Miyajima, Osaka and Kyoto. Two days before you fly, it goes straight into the suitcase.
steps: About 35 minutes from Shinjuku. A slow start after Disney.

Eight hundred metres of nothing but kitchen equipment, where Tokyo’s restaurants buy their tools. We go to the knife shops that sharpen in the window, you hold half a dozen until one fits your hand, and they engrave your name in the blade while we walk on.
Ten minutes on foot. Tokyo’s oldest temple, the big red lantern, and the old shopping street in front of it — the easiest place in the city to finish the souvenir list.
About 35 minutes, with the knife wrapped and boxed for the flight.
course.moves: Hotel → Tawaramachi about 35 min by train. Kappabashi on foot. Kappabashi → Senso-ji 10 min on foot. Asakusa → hotel about 35 min.
food: A bowl of tempura over rice in a wooden old-town building. The queue moves fast and the menu is one dish.
Beef cooked at your table in a private tatami room. The evening to spend a little, two days before you fly home.
A street of tiny grills under awnings, where people sit outside with a beer and a plate of something skewered. Warm evening, no reservation, easy to leave early.
course.good: The one errand on your list that genuinely belongs at the end of the trip. Sitting down for dinner at the end of it.
course.mind: Knives must go in checked baggage, so we box it for the flight. Kappabashi shops close around 17:00, which is why we start at two.

course.name: Shinjuku, without going anywhere
course.tag: The rest day, with a view
course.why: Eighteen days in, the day after twelve hours at DisneySea, and the day before the opera and dinner in Odaiba. This is the version that asks almost nothing of you: no train, no ticket, and you can turn back to the hotel at any point.
steps: Walk to the Metropolitan Government Building
Ten minutes from the hotel lobby, mostly under cover.
Free, no ticket, a lift straight to the top. On a clear October morning Fuji is on the west side of the floor, and the whole route you have just travelled is somewhere in that view.
Tempura fried in front of you at the counter, in a Shinjuku shop that opened in 1924.
A 58-hectare garden with three gardens inside it: a Japanese pond garden, a French formal one and an English lawn. Benches everywhere. We sit as much as we walk.
On foot, in time for a nap before dinner.
course.moves: All of it on foot from the hotel. Observatory 10 min. Observatory → Tsunahachi 12 min. Tsunahachi → Gyoen 10 min. Gyoen → hotel 15 min, or a five-minute taxi.
food: Counter seats, one piece at a time, straight from the oil. The dependable choice in a neighbourhood full of noise.
Shinjuku · grilled skewers in an alley
Sixty tiny bars in two narrow lanes left over from the 1940s, six seats each. Best at dusk, and thirty seconds from the station.
No shame in it on day eighteen. I can book a table downstairs and leave you to it.
course.good: Nothing to book, nothing to catch, and the whole thing is cancellable that morning if you would rather sleep.
course.mind: Honestly: doing nothing at all on Oct 6 is also a good answer. See the note below.

course.name: Ginza, on foot from the table
course.tag: Stationery, a food hall, a rooftop garden, tea
course.why: This goes with any of the five lunches. You stand up from the table and the afternoon is already around you: everything below is inside one neighbourhood, flat, and about two kilometres end to end, with a seat every forty minutes. It is the shopping afternoon — paper, pens, a food hall, sweets to carry back — with a garden on a roof in the middle of it. From lunch 4 in Nihonbashi it starts with a ten-minute taxi; from the others you walk.
steps: Twelve floors of paper and pens in one narrow building, since 1904. Letter sets, washi paper, fountain pens, wrapping — gifts that pack flat. There is a café on the top floor if you want to sit before you start.

Five minutes down the main street. Two floors under the department store of wagashi, tea, pickles, rice crackers and bento from every part of Japan, most of it boxed to travel. The easiest place in Tokyo to buy food gifts, and I translate the counters.
The bakery that invented the sweet-bean bun in 1874, on the corner of the Ginza crossing under the clock tower. A paper bag of five for the hotel room.

A department store with a garden on top, free, open to anyone. Benches, trees, and the whole of Ginza below you. Then the art bookshop on the sixth floor, which is worth a look even if you buy nothing.

On the fourth floor of the same building: a tea house from Uji, near Kyoto, that has been selling matcha since 1854. A bowl of tea, or a matcha jelly and ice cream, sitting down. This is the rest before the walk home.

Seven minutes on, in Ginza 8-chome, a small shop that has sold Japanese folk craft since 1933: hand-made ceramics, textiles, and the wooden kokeshi dolls and small painted toys from country workshops. If the little dolls Linda bought before are what you like, this is the Ginza shop for them. Open Monday 11:00–19:00.
About eight minutes on foot from Takumi, or a five-minute taxi.
course.moves: Lunch → Itoya on foot (5–15 min, or a 10-min taxi from Nihonbashi). Itoya → Mitsukoshi 5 min. Mitsukoshi → Kimuraya across the crossing. Kimuraya → Ginza Six 5 min. Ginza Six → Takumi 7 min. Takumi → hotel about 8 min on foot or a short taxi.
food: Uji tea house since 1854. Matcha whisked in front of you, or the matcha jelly with ice cream and red beans, about ¥1,000–1,800. Open Monday 10:30–20:30.
Soft bread around sweet red bean paste, a cherry blossom pressed into the top, since 1874. About ¥200 each; a bag of five travels fine to the hotel.
Wagashi, tea, pickles and bento from all over Japan, boxed to carry — the place to buy food gifts. Open Monday 10:00–20:00.
course.good: No trains, no taxis unless you want one, and the day ends within sight of your hotel. The right afternoon for a couple who like shops and a kitchen more than a shrine.
course.mind: Everything here is open on Monday the 5th; nothing needs booking. If at four o’clock you would rather have a garden than a bookshop, Hama-rikyu — a 400-year-old shogun’s garden with a tea house on the pond — is a fifteen-minute walk south, last entry 16:30, ¥300. Say so on the day and we go there instead.

course.name: Kappabashi, and the old temple next door
course.tag: Kitchen street, food samples, Senso-ji
course.why: This goes with any of the five lunches. Kappabashi is Tokyo's restaurant-supply street — knives, tableware, and the workshops that make the plastic food models you have seen in every restaurant window. From lunch it is one direct train, no changes. You make a food sample of your own first, walk the street, then Tokyo’s oldest temple ten minutes away on foot with a three-hundred-year-old street of stalls in front of it, and a taxi home.
steps: The Ginza line from Ginza or Nihonbashi station straight to Tawaramachi, about 20 minutes, sitting down. Lunch 1 and 5 are a five-minute walk to Ginza station; lunch 4 is on top of Nihonbashi station.

At Ganso Shokuhin Sample-ya, the shop that popularised the craft in 1932. A booked 40-minute session making a piece of wax tempura or a lettuce leaf, which you keep. I book the Monday slot in advance.

A few hundred metres of restaurant-supply shops: knives that can be engraved with your name while you wait, lacquerware, ceramics by the piece, and the original food-model shops. Most shops are open Mondays — it is Sundays that are quiet here.

Ten minutes from the street. Tokyo’s oldest temple, founded in 628: in under the five-metre paper lantern, along Nakamise — a street of rice-cracker and fan stalls that has been a shopping street for three hundred years — to the main hall. Near the temple end is Sukeroku, a shop the size of a cupboard that has sold tiny hand-made Edo toys and dolls since 1866, for anyone who likes the small kokeshi kind of thing. Flat, with benches in the courtyard.
Melon bread out of the oven, or a bag of hot senbei, eaten as we walk back to the gate.
About 25 minutes across the city, sitting down.
course.moves: Lunch → Ginza or Nihonbashi station on foot, then the Ginza line to Tawaramachi, about 20 min. Tawaramachi → Ganso Sample-ya 12 min on foot. On foot along Kappabashi. Kappabashi → Senso-ji 10 min on foot. Asakusa → hotel about 25 min by taxi.
food: Ganso Shokuhin Sample-ya · made by you
A wax tempura piece or lettuce leaf you make yourself in the 40-minute workshop — not edible, but yours to keep. About ¥3,300 per person. Open Monday 10:00–17:30, no closing day.
Melon bread, grilled rice crackers, sweet bean cakes shaped like the temple gate. A few hundred yen each, eaten standing.
course.good: The afternoon with something you make yourself and something to wrap and take home. Rougher and older than Ginza, with the temple at the end of it.
course.mind: Kappabashi shops mostly close Sundays, so Monday the 5th is a normal day there. The food-sample workshop needs a reservation — I book it as soon as you choose this course and confirm the Monday afternoon slot. This one ends with a taxi rather than a walk, and about half an hour later than Ginza.

course.name: 品川
course.tag: 駅から3分。劇場も店もホテルの敷地で完結
course.why: 品川プリンスホテルの中にある劇場です。品川駅の高輪口を出て坂を上がればすぐで、観たあとの店も同じ敷地にあります。移動が一番少ないのがこのコース。
steps: 品川駅の高輪口から歩いて3分。品川プリンスホテル アネックスタワーの中です。
回の時刻が出たら確定します。チケットはユウキが取ります。
ホテルの敷地内なので、外に出ずに店まで行けます。
course.moves: 品川駅 高輪口 → 劇場 徒歩3分。劇場 → 店 徒歩3分。
course.good: 移動を最小にしたい日。雨予報の日。IMAXで観たい場合もここ。
course.mind: ホテルの敷地は広いので、集合は劇場の入口前にします。ビュッフェは混む時間帯があります。

course.name: 川崎
course.tag: 映画館も店も、ひとつの広場の中にある
course.why: イタリアの街並みを模したラ チッタデッラという広場の中にある映画館です。音の設備に力を入れている劇場なので、ライブの場面がある作品と相性がいい。店も同じ広場の中から選べます。
steps: 川崎駅の東口から歩いて5分。ラ チッタデッラの広場を入ってすぐです。
回の時刻が出たら確定します。
店は広場を出ずに歩いて1分です。
course.moves: 川崎駅 東口 → チネチッタ 徒歩5分。劇場 → 店 徒歩1分。
course.good: 映画のあとに歩き回りたくない日。広場そのものが気持ちいいので、昼まで居られる。
course.mind: 土日の広場はイベントで混みます。10/23は金曜なので比較的静かなはずです。

course.name: 横浜
course.tag: 桜木町駅前のビルの6階。ランチはJRで1駅の崎陽軒本店
course.why: 桜木町駅の目の前、コレットマーレの6階にある劇場です。観たあとはJRで1駅の横浜駅へ移動して、東口の崎陽軒本店でランチ。駅から店までは歩いて3分です。
steps: 桜木町駅の改札前に集合
JR桜木町駅の改札を出たところ。劇場はコレットマーレの6階で、駅から歩いて1分です。
回の時刻が出たら確定します。
JRで横浜駅まで1駅3分。東口に出て崎陽軒本店へ歩いて3分。
course.moves: 桜木町駅 → 劇場 徒歩1分。劇場 → 桜木町駅 → JRで1駅（3分）→ 横浜駅 東口 → 崎陽軒本店 徒歩3分。
course.good: そのあと横浜で遊びたい日。みなとみらいも中華街も電車ですぐです。
course.mind: コレットマーレは桜木町駅の東口（みなとみらい側）を出て正面。ムビチケの発券は6階の発券機でユウキがまとめてやります。

course.name: Akihabara, top to bottom
course.tag: The district, floor by floor
course.why: One day in the anime and manga district, done properly: the big buildings everyone knows and the small shops most visitors never find. No queues for tickets, just walking and browsing.
steps: Electric Town exit. A quick map of the district and what each street is for.
Ten floors of figures, trading cards and model kits. The best place to see what is popular this month.
Eight floors of used manga, animation cels, vintage toys. Prices are honest and the finds are real.
Retro games and the back streets
Super Potato and the second-floor shops, where the district still looks like 2005.
Thirty minutes, one drink. It is part of the culture, and it is fun.
The shrine that blesses electronics, ten minutes uphill. Anime-themed ema plaques and a quiet end to the day.
Evening free. Akihabara is loud until 20:00 if anyone wants more.
course.moves: Everything is on foot. About 3 km over the day, with plenty of sitting.
food: Rich pork broth on the main street since 1984. Fast, loud, and exactly what the district eats.
Handmade buckwheat noodles in an old wooden shop, ten minutes from the station. Quiet and very Tokyo.
course.good: Fans of any depth. Shoppers. Anyone who wants to see the district with someone who knows it.
course.mind: Sundays the main street is closed to cars and busier. Many shops open at 11:00, so mornings start with the big buildings.

course.name: Tokiwa-so and Ikebukuro
course.tag: Where manga was born
course.why: The morning is the apartment where Tezuka, Fujiko Fujio and the other masters lived and drew in the 1950s, rebuilt exactly. The afternoon is Ikebukuro, the district that today serves fans as well as Akihabara does.
steps: Shiinamachi, 20 minutes from Ikebukuro. The rebuilt 1952 apartment: the four-and-a-half-mat rooms, the shared kitchen, the stairs. Free entry, reserved slot.
The neighbourhood monuments, the manga road, and the Chinese restaurant from the stories, still open.
Nine floors, the biggest anime shop in the world. Merchandise, books, the events floor.
The street of second-hand shops (K-Books, Lashinbang) where rare goods surface first.
In Sunshine City, five minutes away. Good for families and for gifts.
course.moves: Train Ikebukuro → Shiinamachi 5 min, then a 15-minute walk to the museum. Back to Ikebukuro by train. Afternoon on foot.
food: The restaurant the Tokiwa-so artists ordered from, and drew into their manga. The same family runs it.
The line outside is the review. Thick pork broth, big portions, twenty minutes from ordering to done.
course.good: Guests who want the history, not only the shopping. Good pacing after a full Akihabara day.
course.mind: Tokiwa-so museum is closed on Mondays. Entry is free but reserved in advance.

course.name: Ghibli Museum and Nakano Broadway
course.tag: Ghibli, then the collectors’ arcade
course.why: The Ghibli Museum is the one place on the trip that needs planning months ahead, and it is worth it. The afternoon is Nakano Broadway, the arcade where Mandarake started, for original cels and rare comics.
steps: Mitaka. Timed entry, tickets bought on the 10th of the previous month. The short film in the Saturn Theater, the Catbus room, the robot on the roof.
Straw Hat Cafe and Inokashira Park
Lunch at the museum cafe, then a walk through the park to Kichijoji station.
Four floors and thirty specialist shops: animation cels, vintage manga, watches, toys. Mandarake’s original home.
The eight-flavour soft serve in the basement. A Nakano rite of passage.
Nakano is five minutes from Shinjuku for the evening.
course.moves: Train to Mitaka 30 min from Shinjuku, then a 15-minute walk or the museum bus. Kichijoji → Nakano 10 min by train.
food: Inside the museum. Simple, good food: the omelette, the cutlet sandwich, the museum beer. Terrace tables outside.
The tallest soft-serve cone in Tokyo, eight flavours stacked. Tiny stand in the basement food hall.
course.good: Ghibli fans, families, anyone who loves the films. Collectors get their best afternoon here.
course.mind: Ghibli Museum is closed Tuesdays. Tickets sell out in minutes, so the trip dates are set around this day. No photos inside the museum.

course.name: Doraemon, then the bullet train
course.tag: Fujiko F. Fujio Museum to Kyoto
course.why: A morning with Doraemon at the museum built for him in Kawasaki, then the Shinkansen to Kyoto with the luggage already on its way hotel-to-hotel. Evening in the old shopping arcades and Gion.
steps: Suitcases handed to the hotel desk. They arrive at the Kyoto hotel the next day, so the day is carried with a small bag only.
Noborito, 30 min from Shinjuku. Timed entry. Original drawings, the rooftop with Doraemon and the Anywhere Door, the museum cafe.
2 hours 15. Mount Fuji on the right side about 45 minutes in, if the sky is clear.
The 400-year-old food arcade, then the Hanamikoji lanes at dusk. Done by 20:00.
course.moves: Shinjuku → Noborito 30 min. Noborito → Shinagawa 40 min. Shinkansen 2h15. Kyoto Station → hotel by taxi.
food: Museum Cafe at Fujiko F. Fujio Museum
Dishes shaped like the characters, Anki-pan French toast, Dorayaki. Kids and adults both order dessert.
Kyoto’s kitchen: grilled skewers, tamagoyaki, pickles, matcha sweets. Everyone picks their own along 400 metres.
course.good: Families. Anyone who wants the train ride to be part of the trip, not a transfer.
course.mind: The Doraemon museum is closed Tuesdays and needs timed tickets. Shinkansen seats are reserved in advance for the group.

course.name: Kyoto Manga Museum and Uji
course.tag: 50,000 volumes, then matcha
course.why: A former elementary school holding 50,000 manga volumes, read anywhere including the lawn. Then Uji, thirty minutes south: the home town of Kyoto Animation, the Byodo-in temple, and the best matcha in Japan.
steps: The Wall of Manga, 200 metres of shelves in a 1929 school building. Pick a series, sit on the lawn, read. Portrait artists on weekends.
30 minutes on the JR Nara line.
The Phoenix Hall on the 10-yen coin, 1053. The museum next door holds the original phoenix statues.
Uji tea street and Nakamura Tokichi
Matcha parfait, matcha soba, the tea shops along the river.
The Uji river bridges and the streets from Sound! Euphonium, for the fans in the group. Optional.
course.moves: Museum is central, walkable from most hotels. Kyoto → Uji 30 min by JR. Uji on foot.
food: The oldest soba house in Kyoto, ten minutes from the museum. Hourai soba with eight toppings in a quiet old townhouse.
The 1854 tea merchant. Matcha jelly, matcha parfait, and tea to bring home. The garden seats go first.
course.good: Readers. Kyoto Animation fans. Guests who want a calm day between Tokyo and Osaka.
course.mind: The Manga Museum closes Wednesdays. Byodo-in’s Phoenix Hall interior is a timed tour with limited places.

course.name: Tezuka’s hometown, then Osaka
course.tag: Takarazuka to Den Den Town
course.why: The Tezuka Osamu Manga Museum in Takarazuka, where the author of Astro Boy grew up, then Osaka’s own otaku district, Den Den Town, and Dotonbori street food at night.
steps: To the Osaka hotel, arriving the same evening.
The Phoenix at the entrance, Astro Boy, the animation workshop where you can make a short piece yourself.
Den Den Town and Ota Road
Osaka’s Akihabara: figure shops, retro games, the maid cafes of Nipponbashi.
Kushikatsu, okonomiyaki, the Glico sign, the canal lights.
course.moves: Kyoto → Takarazuka 1h by JR. Takarazuka → Namba 50 min. Den Den Town to Dotonbori is a 15-minute walk.
food: Deep-fried skewers, one dip only in the shared sauce. The angry-chef sign is the landmark.
The yamaimo okonomiyaki cooked on the counter in front of you. Small, and worth the wait.
course.good: Guests who want both the origin story and the loud, delicious side of Osaka.
course.mind: The Tezuka museum is closed Wednesdays. Dotonbori lines are shortest before 18:00.

course.name: USJ, or a shopping finale
course.tag: Two ways to finish
course.why: Option A is Universal Studios Japan: Super Nintendo World and the seasonal anime collaborations. Option B is a last day for collectors in Nipponbashi, with overseas shipping arranged from the post office. Then Kansai Airport or the train back to Tokyo.
steps: Early entry for Super Nintendo World. Seasonal collaborations (Jujutsu Kaisen, Detective Conan, Attack on Titan) change every few months.
Mandarake Grand Chaos, the Nipponbashi shops, then boxing and shipping purchases home from the post office.
Pork buns at Namba station, the Osaka thing to eat before a train.
Kansai Airport in 50 minutes by rapid train, or the Shinkansen back to Tokyo in 2 hours 30.
course.moves: Hotel → USJ 20 min by train. Namba → Kansai Airport 50 min. Namba → Shin-Osaka 15 min for the Shinkansen.
food: Steamed pork buns made in front of the counter since 1945. Everyone in Osaka carries the white box.
Big octopus pieces, crisp outside, soft inside, cooked at the stand. Eight for the price of a coffee.
course.good: Families choose A. Collectors choose B. Both end at the airport on time.
course.mind: USJ Express passes for Nintendo World sell out early. Shipping from Japan Post takes 1 to 2 weeks by air.

steps: Hikari 640, ordinary car 13, seats 1D and 1E. About an hour to Tokyo.
I’ll be waiting on the platform, right at the door closest to your seats. Message me on WhatsApp if anything changes.

A showroom for museum-quality digital art printing: the craftsmanship and technology behind fine art prints, plus a live printing demonstration up close. 2-16-7 Ginza, Shochiku Building, Chuo-ku · 03-6264-7718. About an hour, with me interpreting.
If you want to see frames for the print before lunch, K.Itoya’s frame corner is a 6-minute walk from FLAT LABO — about 1,500 frame samples and 500 mat samples, B1 floor. Google Maps ↗
One of the five picks below, decided on the day.

A shopping street for professional-grade kitchen tools and restaurant supplies — Japanese knives, ceramics, and the realistic food replicas restaurants use. Popular with chefs and food enthusiasts alike.
Yanaka, Nezu and Sendagi: quiet lanes of old wooden houses, local shops and artisan boutiques, and Yanaka Ginza, lively with street food and small eateries. A glimpse of old Tokyo.
I’ll help with check-in, and that’s where the guided day ends. The suitcase sent ahead from Shizuoka will be waiting for you. Evening free, dinner on your own.
course.moves: Tokyo Station → Ginza about 15 minutes by train, one IC card tap. Ginza → Kappabashi about 40 minutes by train. Kappabashi → Yanesen about 20 minutes by train. Yanesen → Sunshine City Prince Hotel about 30 minutes by train.
food: The Ginza restaurant that invented the pork cutlet and the rice omelette — Japan’s own take on Western food, not the diner version you know.
Tendon, a tempura rice bowl fried to order, in a shop that has been doing exactly this since the Meiji era.
A thick, sweet-savory rolled omelette grilled fresh and handed over on a stick — street food, not scrambled eggs.
Freshwater eel, grilled over charcoal and glazed, served on rice — richer and smokier than anything called “eel” back home.
A bowl piled high with uni over rice — more of it, and fresher, than sea urchin ever gets served in the US.
course.good: Kappabashi and Yanesen are both made for browsing and street food — bring an appetite and a little cash for small shops.
course.mind: Tokyo is still warm in September, so bring water and comfortable walking shoes. Please send FLAT LABO your image files ahead of time for the live printing demonstration.

course.name: Workshop first, then the shops
course.tag: Draw at 13:00, shop until 18:30
course.why: Start with the two hour manga workshop while everyone is fresh, then the shopping is the reward. We meet at the school and the day ends at the station side, close to the trains for your dinner reservation. The school recommends the 13:00 class for families.
steps: We meet at the school door at 12:55. Two hours of drawing manga with a working manga artist, English interpretation included. Nicholas draws his own character and takes the pages home.
About 8 minutes on foot along Sunshine 60 Street.
Mugiwara Store and Pokémon Center Mega Tokyo
Sunshine City, Alpa 2F. The official One Piece store and Japan's largest Pokémon Center are on the same floor. Open to 20:00 on Sunday.
Gashapon Department Store and the One Piece Card Game shop
World Import Mart 3F, same building. Over 3,000 capsule toy machines, then Bandai Namco Cross Store with the official One Piece Card Game shop and Tamashii Nations figures. Open to 21:00.
Two floors of second hand manga, figures, anime goods and Pokémon cards. One Piece volumes in Japanese are everywhere. Open to 22:00.
Nine floors, one of the biggest anime shops in Japan. New manga, figures and limited goods across every series. Open to 21:00.
B2F of PARCO, right at the East Exit. The official Weekly Shonen Jump store: One Piece next to Naruto and Dragon Ball, with items sold nowhere else. Open to 21:00.
Ikebukuro Station East Exit. Dinner at 20:30 is yours.
stops: MANGA DOJO Tokyo 1-31-6 Higashi-Ikebukuro Toshima-ku Tokyo
course.moves: Everything is on foot. Workshop → Sunshine City about 8 min. Sunshine City → Animate about 5 min. Animate → PARCO about 5 min.
course.good: A family that wants the hands-on part done first and a relaxed shopping run after.
course.mind: The 13:00 class is open on December 20 and is the one the school recommends for families. Shopping bags get heavy by the end, so the last two stops are short. Most stores have a tax free counter, so keep your passports with you.

course.name: Toyosu, Tsukiji, then Ginza on foot
course.tag: Auction at 5:30, lunch at 12:00, done about 15:30
course.why: The early part is all near the market and you do it at your own pace. After lunch everything is in Ginza, flat and on foot, and it ends a short walk from your hotel.
steps: Check-in at the PR corner, Block 7, 3F. Reception number 53241. Ends about 6:25.
Sushi or a seafood bowl in the market restaurant area.
Premium Pass x2. Show the QR at the Information Center, no queue. About 1.5 hours.
Taxi, about 15 minutes. Tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, kitchen knives.
Lunch at Ginza Sushimasa, with Yuuki
Counter for three. Short lunch courses: 5 small dishes and 7 pieces of nigiri (¥9,900), or 7 pieces with a small chirashi bowl (¥4,950). We choose at the table.
Twelve floors of paper, pens and letter sets. Gifts that pack flat.
Wagashi, tea, rice crackers and boxed sweets from all over Japan.
The bakery that made the first sweet bean bun, in 1874. On the Ginza crossing.
GINZA SIX roof garden and tea
A free garden on the roof, then matcha at Nakamura Tokichi on the 4th floor.
About 10 minutes on foot to THE BLOSSOM HIBIYA.
course.moves: Market → teamLab: 1 stop on the Yurikamome or a 5 min taxi. teamLab → Tsukiji: taxi about 15 min. Tsukiji → Sushimasa: 10 min on foot. Everything after lunch is on foot.
course.good: A full day that never needs a long train ride.
course.mind: The Ginza walk after lunch is a suggestion. If you would rather rest, we stop whenever you like. Lunch is ordered at the table; the booking is for seats only.

course.name: Meiji Jingu, Harajuku, Shibuya
course.tag: Pickup 9:00, finish time to confirm
course.why: The shrine is calmest in the morning, so it comes first. Harajuku and Omotesando are a short walk downhill from it, and Shibuya is the next station. Lunch goes in the middle so the afternoon is short.
steps: Lobby of THE BLOSSOM HIBIYA. Chiyoda line to Meiji-jingumae, about 20 minutes.
The forest shrine. Free, flat gravel paths, about an hour and a quarter.
The narrow street of teenage fashion and crepe stands, then the wide tree-lined avenue below it. Coffee if you want it.
About 20 minutes on foot down Cat Street. See the crossing from above first, then walk across it.

Kamiyama, a small quiet soba house in the back streets of Shibuya, about 10 minutes on foot from the crossing. 13:00 is after the office lunch rush. Lunch until 14:00. Backup: Tamawarai near Harajuku, open to 15:00.
Tell Yuuki what time you want to finish. If you have energy, Kappabashi kitchen street is one train from Shibuya on the Ginza line, no changes.
course.moves: Hotel → Meiji-jingumae: Chiyoda line, about 20 min. Shrine → Takeshita Street → Omotesando → Shibuya: on foot. Crossing → Kamiyama: 10 min on foot. Shibuya → Kappabashi: Ginza line to Tawaramachi, about 30 min.
course.good: The three things you asked for, in an order that keeps the walking short.
course.mind: The finish time is not fixed yet. Tell Yuuki before the day or in the morning. Kappabashi shops close around 17:00, so it only fits if you finish late.

course.tag: 遠いけれど温泉テーマパーク。1日がかり
course.why: 新宿から越生まで電車で約1時間30分。着いてからは水着で入るサウナ3種と大浴場、岩盤浴、レストランまでそろった施設で、午後を丸ごと使います。
steps: 映画 バイオハザード 吹替 10:25〜12:10
シアター1。R15+。本編94分。公式の表示は終映12:10です。
副都心線で池袋へ、東武東上線急行で坂戸、東武越生線に乗り換え。13:52に越生着、921円、乗換2回。終映から14分なので、間に合わなければ12:40に池袋発の東上線が同じ坂戸行きです。
公式の案内は車やタクシーで約10分。送迎バスは、時刻表に14:20（越生駅西口）の便がありますが、駅発かどうかが表から読み切れません。確実なのはタクシーです。電話 049-292-7889。
おふろPark おごせ 到着・入館
埼玉県入間郡越生町上野3083-1。入館料は土日祝で1,980円（おごせの湯・水着スパ込み）。岩盤浴は+550円で最終受付18:30。水着550円、タオル380円。昼ごはんは館内のレストラン MORINIWA か本館（営業時間は公式ページで確認できていません）。
ユズのキューゲルサウナ、梅のドライサウナ、ハーブのスチームサウナ。水着スパは21:30まで、おごせの湯は22:00まで。

course.name: Akihabara core: 3 hours
course.tag: Retro games, old manga and toys, close to the station
course.why: For the first day after the flight. Three stops, short walks, and a place to sit on the top floor of Super Potato. It is built around the 1990s shonen and game shelves, which suits Dragon Ball Z, Digimon, Cowboy Bebop, Mario and Zelda.
steps: We meet here. Radio Kaikan is across the street, so there is almost no walking to start. If you are tired, tell me and we slow down.
Ten floors facing the station. We take the lift to the top and walk down. Figures and toys are on 3F to 7F, and K-BOOKS is on 3F.

Famicom to PlayStation 2 on the 3rd and 4th floors, plus handhelds and Sega. The early Mario and Zelda games are on the Famicom and Super Famicom shelves. The 5th floor is a small retro arcade with a place to sit.
Boys' manga and vintage books on 3F. Toys on 6F to 8F, with Chogokin on 7F and robots on 8F. Stock changes every week, so we see what is there that day. We finish here at 13:00.
course.moves: All on foot, about ten minutes at most between shops. Radio Kaikan is across the street from the station, and Mandarake is about four minutes from the Electric Town exit.
course.good: A slow first day: a few shops, one tall building of toys, and somewhere to sit.
course.mind: Check that a Japanese game runs on your console at home, and on 100 V power, before you buy. A Famicom cartridge does not fit an NES without an adapter.

course.name: Akihabara deep: 5 hours
course.tag: Gunpla and model shops, retro games, lunch and Mandarake
course.why: For the most of Akihabara in one day. It keeps everything in course A and adds the Gunpla and model shops, a sit-down lunch and a longer stay at Mandarake. Good if Gundam Wing is high on the list.
steps: We meet here. Yodobashi is one minute away, so the first shop is almost at the door.
Plastic models, modelling tools, figures and games are all on the 6th floor. A good first look at the current Gunpla kits.
Ten floors facing the station. Kaiyodo is on 5F, Yellow Submarine with its model kits on 6F, and Volks on 8F. We take the lift to the top and walk down.
Famicom to PlayStation 2 on the 3rd and 4th floors, plus handhelds and Sega. The 5th floor is a small retro arcade with a place to sit.
The figure and model kit maker's own shop. It sells new releases and shop-only items, and the pop-ups change, so we see what is on that week.

Kanazawa curry: a pork cutlet on a dark, thick roux, eaten at the counter. It is quick and close to the station. If you would rather sit down for a steak, Juke Steak serves lunch and I can swap it in.
Boys' manga and vintage books on 3F. Toys on 6F to 8F, with Chogokin on 7F and robots on 8F. Stock changes every week, so we see what is there that day.
Seven floors of kits, figures and goods. Volks's own kits are on 4F, and the 6th and 7th floors host pop-up events that change. We finish here around 15:00.
course.moves: All on foot. Most legs are short, and the longest is from lunch to Mandarake. We work from the station south to Kotobukiya, then north.
course.good: Gunpla and figure fans who want the whole district in one day, with a proper lunch in the middle.
course.mind: Go!Go!Curry takes cash only, so bring some for the smaller shops too. The Dragon Ball Store is not in Akihabara: it is on the 1st floor of Tokyo Station Ichibangai, two stops away, and I can add it if you want it.

course.name: Akihabara and Shibuya: full day
course.tag: Akihabara in the morning, Nintendo and Pokémon in the afternoon
course.why: For both worlds. The morning is the short version of course A, and the afternoon is Shibuya for Mario, Zelda and Pokémon, with Nintendo TOKYO and the Pokémon Center on one floor.
steps: We meet here. Radio Kaikan is across the street.
Ten floors facing the station. We take the lift to the top and walk down. Figures and toys are on 3F to 7F.
Famicom to PlayStation 2 on the 3rd and 4th floors. The early Mario and Zelda games are on the Famicom and Super Famicom shelves. The 5th floor is a small retro arcade.
Kanazawa curry at the counter, quick and close to the station. An early lunch, so we are not hunting for food in Shibuya.
About 30 to 40 minutes by train. I ride with you and tell you which line to take.

Nintendo's own store on the 6th floor of Shibuya PARCO, five minutes on foot from Shibuya Station. On busy days entry is by numbered ticket, and a weekday is calmer. I check the store's page that morning.
The official Pokémon store, on the same floor. Thirty to forty-five minutes is enough for most people.
Official Weekly Shonen Jump goods, also on the 6th floor. Dragon Ball is one of the series the Jump Shops cover, and what is in stock changes.
One basement floor in the Shibuya BEAM building, five minutes from the Hachikō exit. Shonen comics, vintage comics and toys. We finish here around 17:00.
course.moves: Akihabara on foot in the morning, then one train ride of about 30 to 40 minutes. In Shibuya the three PARCO stores share one floor, and Mandarake is a five-minute walk away.
course.good: Nintendo and Pokémon fans who also want the Akihabara shelves, and do not mind one train ride.
course.mind: Shibuya PARCO has irregular closing days, so I check its calendar the week before. New Pokémon card products are sold by advance lottery, so sealed packs are unlikely, but the store is worth it for everything else. A Gundam Base is announced for the 5th floor of the same building from November 2026, and I will check whether it has opened.
